Learning objective

Identify hazards and select a safe next action.

Explanation

A hazard is a source of possible harm; risk considers how harm could occur and its consequences. Before work, look for damaged cables, wet areas, unstable access, falling objects, traffic, heavy loads and blocked exits. A neat-looking site can still contain hidden services or energized equipment.

Synthetic example

A loose cable crosses a busy walkway. The exercise asks for a controlled routing solution and communication, not merely a warning shouted once.

Practical exercise

Identify three hazards in a fictional storeroom and propose one safer alternative for each.

lessons.title: Electrical and equipment awareness
objectives: Recognize when equipment must be left to qualified personnel.
explanation: Thailand has specific occupational electrical-safety regulations and training requirements; the DLPW reference index links the regulation and notices. A short online lesson is not that qualification. Do not open energized equipment, defeat guards or improvise repairs. Unexpected heat, burning smell, exposed conductors or liquid ingress require a safe stop and qualified assessment.

Network equipment can still be connected to mains supplies, backup power or other energy sources. Switching off one visible switch does not prove all energy is isolated. Isolation, verification and re-energization belong to trained authorized personnel using the approved method. Handle equipment using rated lifting and carrying methods; inspect packaging, connectors and manufacturer instructions without creating exposure.
lessons.example: A recorder emits a burning smell. Keep people clear and seek the site emergency/qualified response; do not open the enclosure to inspect it.
lessons.exercise: Sort actions into safe observation versus work requiring authorization.
lessons.model_response: Safe from a protected location: record model and reported symptom. Requires qualified authorization: opening a mains supply or proving isolation.
key_points: A network device can have hazardous energy

lessons.title: Height PPE and handling
objectives: Explain why access and rescue planning precede height work.
explanation: Consider whether work can be done from the ground. Where height work remains necessary, competent people must plan suitable access, fall prevention, equipment inspection and emergency arrangements. A harness alone does not make an unsafe setup acceptable. Ladders are not a universal solution, and a chair is not access equipment.

Select PPE for the assessed hazard, correct fit and compatibility. Inspect it and follow its instructions; damaged equipment should not be used. Do not attach fall protection to an unverified anchor. Keep people clear of falling-object areas and use approved handling arrangements. The learner’s exercise is a paper planning review; it includes no climbing, lifting experiment or live installation.
lessons.example: A camera is above a stairwell. The safe planning response considers another mounting arrangement or properly assessed access, not balancing a ladder on a step.
lessons.exercise: List the missing planning information before a fictional high-level camera installation.
lessons.model_response: Access method, competent personnel, site assessment, fall prevention, exclusion area, equipment suitability and rescue arrangements.
lessons.thai_summary: พิจารณาทำงานจากพื้นก่อน อุปกรณ์ป้องกันส่วนบุคคลไม่ทดแทนการวางแผนทางขึ้น การป้องกันการตก และการช่วยเหลือ
lessons.summary: Avoid height exposure where possible PPE does not replace planning No climbing in this exercise

lessons.title: Incidents site conduct and quality
objectives: Record observations and maintain professional site boundaries.
explanation: If an incident or near miss occurs, protect yourself, seek the designated emergency response and avoid disturbing the scene except where necessary for immediate safety. Do not attempt a rescue beyond your training. Record time, location, observed conditions and witnesses through the verified reporting route. Do not speculate about blame or publish images of people.

At a customer site, confirm access permission, work boundaries and the approved scope. Protect property, keep routes clear and obtain permission before taking evidence photographs. Quality assurance means building reliable checks into the process; final inspection alone cannot repair every planning failure. Record incomplete work and unresolved risks truthfully so that the next person can act.
lessons.example: A box falls near a colleague without injury. Treat the near miss as useful safety information rather than hiding it because nobody was hurt.
lessons.exercise: Write a four-line near-miss report using fictional facts.
lessons.model_response: At 10:20 a loosely stacked box fell in aisle B. No injury observed. Area access was restricted safely. Supervisor review of stacking controls requested.
key_points: Report near misses as well as harm
lessons.thai_summary: รายงานเหตุเกือบเกิดอุบัติเหตุและข้อบกพร่องตามช่องทางที่ยืนยันแล้ว เคารพพื้นที่ลูกค้าและบันทึกข้อจำกัดตามจริง
